ownership_decision.invariant: Workspace Activity owns only contracted source coverage, completeness, global ordering, cursor semantics and typed continuation composition. Identity resolves only the authenticated Session's Workspace. Run, Evaluation, Creation, Packaging and Publishing remain authoritative for their own Activity classifications, timestamps, stable source identities and continuation identifiers. Activity may merge owner-produced facts with the fixed priority needs_attention before in_progress before recent before neutral, but it never interprets an owner's raw status or becomes a lifecycle owner.

boundary_decision.interaction: Run, Evaluation, Creation, Packaging and Publishing each produce a versioned, narrow Workspace-scoped fact-reader contract consumed by the Workspace Activity query Context through composition-root injection. Run and Evaluation facts are joined by platform run_id only after both owners have classified their own states. Activity queries all five readers with the Session-derived Workspace, performs a deterministic priority merge and global keyset merge, reports source coverage, and maps typed continuation identifiers to transport without importing lifecycle owners into one another.
boundary_decision.consistency: Synchronous live reads with no persisted Activity Context. Pagination is stable for an unchanged dataset and does not claim a cross-request snapshot. Any contracted reader failure fails closed with HTTP 503, complete=false and unavailable_sources, without items or a cursor. Reads are idempotent and the client retries the complete request.
prohibited_dependencies: composition-owned interpretation of lifecycle or evaluation raw statuses
cross-context SQL or generated query row sharing
one lifecycle Context importing another to build Activity
Activity owning or reclassifying a source lifecycle state
analytics or trace events used as lifecycle truth
clock-derived Artifact expiry represented as a persisted Activity event
Catalog exposure or Bundle Publication inferred into first-version Publication Activity
silent omission of an unavailable contracted source

domain_forces: Returning creators need one place to resume long work without creating a second state machine or losing the exact source object.
Run execution and Evaluation verdict are separate owner facts even though the user experiences them as one Run item.
Creation pending actions, Artifact defensive scan states, Artifact availability, Publication status, Release recency and Catalog exposure have different owners or time semantics.
A cross-source workbench needs one authorization boundary, total ordering, explicit source coverage and failure semantics that independent browser queries cannot provide.
Current source lists use incompatible offset, capped or name-based ordering and cannot prove global continuation.
The current Run-only UI must keep its scope disclosure until every contracted owner fact and failure path is proven.
implementation_design.decision: Introduce Workspace Activity as a query-only Context with no Aggregate, event stream or persisted projection. Add only the source timestamp current data cannot prove: Run activity_updated_at. Packaging uses Artifact created_at because its current standard flow creates the Artifact and reaches available in one transaction; quarantined and rejected remain defensive needs_attention states rather than a claimed background workflow. Identity supplies the Workspace; Run, Evaluation, Creation, Packaging and Publishing each return minimal owner facts through five versioned internal contracts. Activity combines Run and Evaluation by stable platform run_id using only the fixed classification priority, then performs a five-reader fail-closed fan-in and deterministic global keyset merge. The public endpoint is GET /me/activity. The first item kinds are Run, Creation Session, Packaging Artifact and Skill Publication with latest Release; Bundle Publication and Catalog exposure remain outside the first contract. No tactical Aggregate pattern is introduced because Activity owns query semantics, not source lifecycle state.
invariants_preserved: Workspace scope comes from the authenticated Session and is applied by every owner reader.
Each owner remains authoritative for raw status, classification, source identity, update-time meaning and continuation identifiers.
Activity owns source coverage, completeness, global ordering, cursor semantics and continuation envelope, but no source lifecycle state.
Activity is read-only and never changes, repairs or advances source state.
Run lifecycle and Evaluation verdict remain separate axes before mechanical composition.
Artifact scan status and clock-derived availability remain separate facts.
Publication, latest Release, distribution availability, Bundle Publication and Catalog exposure remain separate facts.
Unknown, unavailable, absent and empty remain distinguishable.
rejected_alternatives: A new persisted Activity Context: the requirement is a query projection and does not justify replay, synchronization or another state owner.
Browser-side composition: it cannot establish one authorization boundary, one global cursor or truthful source coverage.
Entrypoint raw-status switches: they would move owner decisions into transport orchestration.
Letting Run classify Evaluation verdicts: Evaluation is a separate reviewed Context, so its verdict meaning stays owner-produced.
A single cross-context SQL query: it bypasses owner Services and couples unrelated schemas.

Using created_at indiscriminately as every source's recency: it loses Run transitions, Evaluation completion, Creation advances and later Releases; Packaging is the deliberate exception because its current standard completion is atomic.

Making Packaging asynchronous merely to manufacture an in_progress Activity state: the product has no observable background scan workflow today, so that would add behavior for presentation rather than domain need.
Treating expires_at as an Activity event: expiry is a deterministic clock boundary, not a recorded owner transition.
Including Bundle Publication because a management entry exists: its distinct item identity and continuation deserve a later explicit contract rather than silent scope expansion.
Treating Catalog exposure as Publishing recency: exposure is a separate operator decision and can change for reasons the creator cannot advance.

contract_change.description: Add GET /me/activity as a Session-authenticated Workspace read endpoint with a stable item envelope, owner-produced classifications, typed continuations, deterministic global keyset cursor and explicit coverage of Run, Evaluation, Creation, Packaging and Publishing readers.
contract_change.compatibility: Additive. Existing lifecycle list endpoints and /workspace/runs remain compatible. Item kind remains a string so an older client can show stable summary fields and an unsupported-kind state without interpreting raw status; known continuations use generated typed variants.
contract_change.data_classification: Workspace-scoped metadata only; excludes Creation Snapshot and prompt, Trace payload, Evaluation verdict text and findings, package contents, download history and exposure review findings.
contract_change.retry_behavior: Read-only and idempotent. Any contracted reader failure returns HTTP 503 with complete=false and unavailable_sources, without items or next_cursor; clients retry the whole read.

record.name: Workspace Activity
record.responsibility: Owns the Workspace-scoped cross-source activity query: contracted source coverage, completeness, global ordering, cursor semantics and typed continuation composition, but no source lifecycle state.

approvals.scope: Unchanged rebased replacement for the explicitly approved v3 scope: query-only Workspace Activity, five owner-produced fact readers, GET /me/activity, backend projection, frontend workbench, tests, documents, and the already approved source-corpus confirmation.
